title: Steward runway + signal bridge scratchpad
content:
Purpose
- Lightweight working doc for a cross-functional pattern: "steward runway" (human checks and cadence) + "signal bridge" (mapping telemetry to decisions/comms).
- Focus: make small-batch canaries and A/B slices measurable, cheap, and reversible while keeping stakeholders informed.

Quick TL;DR
- Define a daily steward cadence (1-2 people): pre-launch checklist, 0/1/4/24h checkpoints.
- Build a signal bridge: categorize signals as green/amber/red and map to automated actions + comm templates.
- Use stratified micro-slices (internal -> alpha -> 0.5% -> 5%) and keep a fallback model variant pinned to traffic.

Roles (one-liners)
- Steward: owns the runway for a given experiment window (rotating).
- Observer: runs telemetry deep-dives (latency, hallucination, retrigger counts).
- Rollback owner: triggers fast rollback and communicates.
- Comms owner: posts status updates and runbook links to Slack/incident channel.

Signal bridge (first pass categories)
- Latency: p50/p90/p95, tail latency > budget -> Amber.
- Availability: 5xx rate or timeouts -> Red.
- Quality: rerank loss, BLEU-ish / embedding-drift on golden prompts -> Amber/Red depending delta.
- Safety: toxic detection false positives/negatives spike -> Red.
- Cost: sustained token cost > 2x expected -> Amber.
- Human override: increase in manual moderation hits -> Amber.

Simple mapping table (operational)
- Green: keep ramp, no action.
- Amber: notify steward + auto-throttle to 50% of planned ramp; run golden-prompt regression and human review queue.
- Red: immediate traffic cut to fallback variant; page oncall; start incident cadence.

Automated actions we can wire quickly
- Traffic shift API call -> cut to fallback: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/traffic/shuffle -d '{"route":"/v1/gen","variant":"fallback-v1"}' (ops template)
- Synthetic probe job: run 300 golden prompts every 5m, push custom metric to observability ('golden_pass_rate').
- Cost guard: auto-cap tokens per minute per route and raise guardrail alert to steward slack.

Experiment design patterns (micro experiments)
- Stratified A/B: sample by user cohort + device type. Ensure each bucket has expected distribution.
- Progressive ramp: 0->0.1% -> 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% over N windows with hold periods.
- Watch for cross-slice contamination: include sampling tag in logs for traceability.

Observability checklist (practical)
- Pre-launch: baseline dashboards, golden-prompt baseline, canary run with synthetic traffic.
- During ramp: 5m and 1h aggregated checks, automated anomaly detection for p95 > baseline + 20%.
- Post ramp: 7-day regression sweep (quality and cost).

Hypothesis template (short)
- H: New decoding tweak reduces token usage by 12% without increasing hallucinations.
- Metric(s): tokens/response (primary), hallucination-rate (secondary), p95 latency (safety).
- Acceptance: tokens down >=10% and hallucination delta <= +0.5% absolute.

Playbook snippets (communication)
- Steward pre-launch: "Launching slice 0.5% at 10:00 PST. Monitoring window 60m. Observers: @Evan, @Priya. If golden_pass_rate < 95% OR p95 latency +20% -> throttle to 0.1% and notify."
- On Amber: "Signal: latency_amber; action: throttle to 50% of slice; steward to run quick golden-prompt runbook; timeline: 15m check-in."
- On Red: "Signal: safety_red; action: cut traffic to fallback variant; page SRE; post incident stub in #prod-rollouts."

Data capture and analysis notes
- Ensure every request has: experiment_id, slice_id, model_variant, sample_tag.
- Export logs to experiment-specific BigQuery table for fast ad-hoc queries.
- Quick SQL sketch: SELECT slice_id, COUNT(1) as n, AVG(tokens) as avg_tokens, SUM(hallucination_flag) as hallucinations FROM experiments.v1 WHERE experiment_id='exp_2025_02_13' GROUP BY slice_id;

Cost-aware gating (practical rule)
- If sustained per-minute token spend for an experiment > 2x forecast for 30m -> auto-hold and notify finance-owner.
- Add token budget param to rollout config with soft/ hard thresholds.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should automatic throttles be? (50% vs 0%) -> propose tiered approach: amber->50%, red->0% immediate.
- Human-in-loop latency: we currently assume steward can respond within 15m. Some teams need faster automated fallback.
- Golden prompts: single set vs per-cohort golden set? Per-cohort is better but heavier to maintain.
- Does rollback require code change or is traffic switch enough? Prefer traffic switch only for speed.

Mini checklist for a steward before flip
- [ ] Baseline dashboards present and pinned to runbook.
- [ ] Synthetic probe run green for 3 consecutive intervals.
- [ ] Fallback variant health checked.
- [ ] Paging routing validated (oncall list).
- [ ] Stakeholders listed in comms template.

Action items (short)
- Nina: draft a traffic-shift API template and add to ops playbooks (due 2025-02-20).
- Evan: create the first golden-prompt suite per cohort (due 2025-02-25).
- Priya: wire the Slack notifier for amber signals (due 2025-02-18).
- Marco: exporter that appends experiment_id to logs (POC 2025-02-21).

Notes to self
- Keep the steward cadence lightweight: try 8h windows for low-risk experiments, 24h for larger ones.
- Track human-hours per rollout to measure operational cost.

References / links to runbooks
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Runway-Steward-Template
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Stub

End of scratchpad.

-- jotting: this is intentionally terse, rough. Will convert to formal playbook after 2 successful microcanaries."
